title: A person who registers no distress at another's suffering can keep harming them, because nothing inside them calls for it to stop
body:
- Empathic distress at another's suffering normally creates an internal cost to causing that suffering, which inhibits further harm.
- A harm-doer who does not register the victim's pain receives no such feedback, so the natural brake on the behavior never fires.
- The deficit can be perceptual (an inability to read the other's emotional state) or cultivated (deliberate indifference); in either form the same corrective signal is missing.
- Without that signal, the harm continues — sustained, "effortless," without guilt or remorse that would prompt the actor to change.
- The pattern can persist indefinitely, because nothing inside the actor calls for it to stop.
- Case: a man inflicting emotional violence on his wife described being "assisted by mindblindness, unaware of her pain," allowing the behavior to continue "effortlessly" without bothering him.
conversion: none — standing condition: the absence of empathic feedback costs the victim the protection their pain would otherwise trigger in the harm-doer.
